records.summary: - Neuro-Conditioning Devices: Advanced tech devices designed to recalibrate brainwaves and dampen cravings, though not without risk. - Craving Suppressant Implant: This device delivers small bursts of neuro-conditioning that grant immunity to cravings for 12 hours. However, each use drains the userʼs vitality, requiring a Resilience Check (DC 15) to avoid a -2 penalty to Strength and Focus for 24 hours. - Mood Stabilizer Patches: Bio-enhanced patches that release mood-stabilizing chemicals, granting a +1 bonus to Willpower Checks for 8 hours. Extended use may cause dependency, imposing a -1 penalty to Willpower for 24 hours after the effects wear off. - Side Effects of Technology: Advanced recovery tech is powerful but taxing on the body. - Tech Dependency: Relying on implants or neuro-conditioning creates a tech dependency. After three consecutive days of use, characters must succeed on a Resilience Check (DC 15) to avoid becoming dependent, needing regular access to the tech to avoid a -2 penalty on Willpower Checks.

Therapeutic support combines natural, psionic, and mystical approaches to ease addiction symptoms temporarily. It involves the use of healing herbs, psionic meditation, and ethereal rituals, which can be accessed by characters depending on the reality they inhabit or their personal resources.

Psionic practitioners use focused mental energy to stimulate rapid cellular repair, closing wounds and mending injuries faster than natural healing. - Healing Effect: A successful Psionic Check (DC 15) restores 2d6 HP to the target. This ability can be used once every 8 hours to gradually recover injuries. - Accelerated Regeneration: Skilled psionics can deepen the level of repair by focusing on specific injuries. By increasing the DC to 18, the healer can restore 3d6 HP and clear minor conditions such as fatigue or minor bruising. - Psychic Exhaustion: Each use of Tissue Regeneration within 24 hours increases the risk of psychic exhaustion. After each use beyond the first, the healer must roll a Resilience Check (DC 15). Failure results in -1 penalty to Willpower until the next rest. - Regenerative Link: The healer may establish a lasting link, boosting natural healing rates. For the next 24 hours, the target regains 1 additional HP per hour of rest. However, the healer cannot use any psionic powers for one hour after setting up this link due to the mental toll. ---

The default penalties for targeting body parts assume average humanoid proportions and difficulty. Consider adjusting based on: •Target Size: Larger or smaller creatures may shift difficulty. E.g., –3 to head for a giant, –8 to hand for a fairy. •Target Movement: Increase penalty if the target is moving quickly or erratically. •Weapon Accuracy: Precision weapons (like sniper rifles) may reduce penalties. Spread-based weapons may make called shots harder or impossible.

records.proposedName: Damage Effects by Hit Location (Optional Advanced Rule)
records.summary: For groups seeking a more detailed and tactical combat experience, this rule allows specific body parts to have unique consequences when hit by a called shot or a critical hit. These effects are in addition to normal damage and are subject to the GMʼs discretion based on the severity of the blow, damage type, and circumstances.

•When attacking a target with cover, the attacker applies the cover bonus to the targetʼs DR, effectively increasing the difficulty to hit. •If the attack misses because of the cover bonus, itʼs assumed to have hit the cover instead. •Attacks that hit cover may damage or destroy it, depending on the material, size, and attack type (at GM discretion).

Reactions are special responses a character can take when triggered by a specific event, typically outside of their normal turn. In ranged and melee combat, reactions can turn the tide by avoiding damage, punishing missed attacks, or protecting allies. ➤ Dodge (Reaction) •Trigger: Declared before an attack is rolled against the character. •Effect: The attacker must reroll their attack and take the lower result (disadvantage). •Cost: Uses the characterʼs reaction for the round. Dodge represents a deliberate attempt to move entirely out of the way. Characters must be aware of the attack and must not be restrained or unaware. ➤ Evade (Reaction) •Trigger: Declared before an attack is rolled. •Effect: The attack hits, but the damage is reduced by the characterʼs Dexterity modifier (minimum 1). •Cost: Uses the characterʼs reaction for the round. Evading is a defensive maneuver that absorbs or redirects part of the incoming force rather than avoiding it outright. ➤ Parry (Reaction – Requires Parry Weapon) •Trigger: A melee attack is made against the character. •Effect: Make a parry roll (d20 + weapon modifier). If this roll meets or beats the attackerʼs roll, the attack is deflected. •Cost: Uses the characterʼs reaction. Only weapons with the Parry property can be used to parry. Some abilities or feats may modify this rule. ➤ Counterattack (Reaction) •Trigger: An enemy misses a melee attack against the character. •Effect: The character immediately makes a single melee attack in retaliation. •Cost: Uses the characterʼs reaction. This aggressive maneuver rewards high-defense or evasive characters who bait enemies into overextending.
•If a critical hit triggers massive damage, the saving throw DC increases by +5. •Rolling a natural 1 on the save results in two rolls on the Injury Table, and the GM chooses the worse result.

💤 Rest Requirements (Short vs Long Rest) •Short Rest: Does not remove exhaustion by default. (Optional abilities or tech may allow partial recovery.) •Long Rest: Reduces one level of exhaustion. A full nightʼs sleep in safe conditions is required. •Multiple Long Rests: Characters suffering from multiple levels must rest for several days, reducing one level per night. ✨ Narrative Tip: Use exhaustion to pace gameplay. Survival journeys, stress-heavy missions, and cursed zones should challenge players to manage fatigue alongside damage.
Fear represents immediate emotional responses to terrifying threats. Horror represents the cumulative mental strain from prolonged or overwhelming exposure.

When encountering frightening stimuli (e.g., horrifying creatures), roll: Fear Check = d20 + Wisdom or Charisma modifier Compare against the Fear DC set by the GM. •Failure triggers a Fear Effect (see Section 3). •Success allows the character to keep their composure.

In areas of lingering dread or twisted reality, Horror builds over time: •Every 10 minutes spent in a high-Horror area increases the Horror DC by 1. •Characters must make periodic Horror Checks: ◦ Success: Avoid Sanity loss. ◦ Failure: Lose 1d4 SP.
A Trigger is a recurring psychological vulnerability tied to a past trauma.

Bonds represent close connections between characters, whether they stem from shared experiences, family ties, rivalries, or romantic attachments. Bonds offer mechanical advantages that grow as the relationship deepens, and they create roleplaying opportunities through specific challenges and roleplay hooks.

Building connections and understanding others on a deep, emotional level. - Description: Empathy is used to relate to others and connect with them emotionally. This skill helps gain trust, comfort others, and understand unspoken concerns. - Mechanics: Roll an Empathy check to build rapport, soothe strong emotions, or gain an ally through genuine connection. - Modifiers: Lower the DC if the character and target share a similar experience. Increase it if the target is suspicious or has opposing motives.

- Rules: Access to guild resources, such as materials or information. Once per week, make a DC 10 Charisma check to receive job offers from guild affiliates. - Penalty: Disadvantage on Charisma checks when dealing with rival guilds.

Imposing your will through fear or commanding presence. - Description: Intimidation is used to instill fear, assert dominance, or compel obedience. This can be done through threatening language, physical displays, or a powerful presence. - Mechanics: Roll an Intimidation check when attempting to make someone comply out of fear, stop a fight, or gain information under duress. - Modifiers: Increase the DC if the target has a strong resolve or if the player is outnumbered. Decrease it if the player has a clear advantage or a significant reputation.

Captivating others through storytelling, music, or physical expression. - Description: Performance is used to entertain, inspire, or emotionally move an audience, whether through music, storytelling, or theater. Itʼs ideal for characters who rely on charisma or creativity to engage others. - Mechanics: Roll a Performance check when you are performing before an audience or trying to leave a memorable impression. - Modifiers: Increase the DC for large audiences or complex performances, and decrease it for familiar or practiced routines.

records.proposedName: How Social Status Effects Affect Gameplay**
records.summary: - **Decision-Making**: Depending on the character's status, players may approach situations differently. A beloved hero might boldly approach the city gates, while a known thief might seek stealthier entrances. - **Resource Availability**: Social status can determine access to resources. A guild member might get premium gear, while an exile might struggle to buy basic goods. - **Interaction Dynamics**: NPCs might treat the character differently. A revered character might receive offers of help, while a disgraced one could be shunned. - **Quest and Story Arcs**: Certain quests or plotlines might be available only if the character possesses a particular status.
